{{Quote|I said I'll take it!|The guard|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] worked as a '''guard''' and an [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]] in the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], the man was on leave on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] shortly before the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], ordered a [[Blockade of Kashyyyk (1 ABY)|blockade]] of the planet. While off duty, the guard paid a visit to a [[Trading post Wookiee Planet C|trading post]] near the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Rwookrrorro/Legends|Rwookrrorro]] and bullied the [[Merchant/Legends|shopkeeper]], [[Saun Dann]], into giving away some of his goods for free. Having successfully pressured Dann, the guard left the trading post with an extorted high-tech [[groomer]] tucked in his [[Belt/Legends|belt]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|No, I'm off duty. I've come to look around your shop.|The guard to Saun Dann|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] served as a [[Security guard/Legends|guards]]<ref name="SWHS" /> and an [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]]<ref name="Cylinders">In ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', he is shown carrying two [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinders]]. In the "Imperial code cylinder" entry of ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', it was stated that such devices were issued to [[Imperial officer/Legends|officers]]&mdash;as opposed to mere enlisted [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]].</ref> in the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]],<ref name="SWHS" /> the armed forces of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="IS">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref> In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="Leland Holiday">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=870#15778940|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-10-12|time=6:13 PM}}</ref> the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], suspected [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] activity on the [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]&mdash;then known as "[[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] Planet C" to the Imperials&mdash;and ordered martial law to be declared there. A [[Blockade of Kashyyyk (1 ABY)|blockade]] was set up around the planet and a curfew was imposed. The [[Officer/Legends|officer]] was on leave on the Wookiee [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] when the [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] started, still wandering about in his in [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Imperial military uniforms/Legends|uniform]].<ref name="SWHS" />

While off duty, the Imperial decided to visit "[[Trading post Wookiee Planet C]]," a local shop<ref name="SWHS" /> located near [[Rwookrrorro/Legends|Rwookrrorro]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of Kashyyyk.<ref name="Rwookrrorro">In the ''Holiday Special'', the trading post was shown to be close to [[Chewbacca's home]], which the novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'' established as being located in Rwookrrorro.</ref> When the [[Merchant/Legends|shopkeeper]], [[Saun Dann]], saw him looking at the merchandise, he was frightened and thought the officer wanted to see his [[Identichip/Legends|identification]]. Dann reached into his pocket to pull out his ID, but the guard stopped him, stating that he was off-duty and only wished to look around the shop. The salesman then attempted to sell him a micro-sized [[Aquarium/Legends|aquarium]]. The black-clad guard inspected the fish inside for a moment before putting the container on the counter, and then bluntly commented that he hated fish, which made Dann more nervous. The old man then retrieved what appeared to be a [[Groomer|hair trimmer]], which he gave to the Imperial in hopes that he would be interested in it.<ref name="SWHS" />

The situation was becoming tense when a beeping sound was issued by a [[wallscreen]]. While Dann spoke with the caller, a female Wookiee named [[Mallatobuck/Legends|Mallatobuck]], the guard continued browsing the goods for sale. The Imperial had been fooled: unbeknownst to him, Saun Dann was really a member of the Rebel Alliance, and Mallatobuck was the wife of [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], one of the Rebellion's heroes the Empire sought to apprehend. The Imperial did not notice Dann looking back to see if he was paying attention to him, nor did he realize that the video conversation was a secret message about Chewbacca and his friend, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]].<ref name="SWHS" />

When the conversation was over, Saun Dann returned to the guard, who told him he was unimpressed with the last item he had been offered to buy. Feeling challenged, the shopkeeper picked up the manual for the groomer and started demonstrating it as he talked. The Imperial finally took the groomer from Dann's hands and put it in his [[Belt/Legends|belt]]. When the old man asked him if he wished to pay or trade for it, the guard answered that he would simply take it. Without any further ado, he walked away with the extorted merchandise, leaving a confused and mumbling Saun Dann alone in his shop.<ref name="SWHS" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Ah, here we are. Here it is. A pocket-sized aquarium. Wonderful, isn't it? And, you can take it with you anywhere. And the tank is a snap to clean.''"<br />"''I hate fish.|Saun Dann and the guard|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
[[File:I_hate_fish-SWHS.png|thumb|left|200px|Saun Dann attempts to sell a pocket-sized fish tank to the black-clad guard.]]
The Imperial guard was a Human of average size and build, with brown [[Hair/Legends|hair]], a bushy mustache and brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. He stared at Saun Dann with cold, intimidating looks and spoke with a deep, growling voice in a military fashion, using short sentences. He would take advantage of his status as an Imperial guard, ready to bully the shopkeeper to obtain what he wished. He was rather blasé about the exotic items Dann attempted to sell him, remaining calm and uninterested the entire [[Time/Legends|time]]. When the shopkeeper left him on his own for a moment, the officer started browsing the merchandise with obvious nonchalance. The mustachioed guard also loathed fishes.<ref name="SWHS" />

==Equipment==
When in service, the guard wore a black double-breasted tunic and a swooping, black-tinted blast [[Armor/Legends|helmet]]<ref name="SWHS" /> made of [[Plastoid/Legends|plastoid]] composite alloy.<ref name="SWVD">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> On both outside panels of his tunic, there were pockets containing code cylinders,<ref name="SWHS" /> devices that allowed officers access to [[Computer/Legends|computer]] systems and secure areas.<ref name="SWVD" /> His belt was also equipped with an [[Officer's disk/Legends|officer's disc]],<ref name="SWHS" /> which contained additional coded information.<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> The guard's issued uniform did not fit him exactly, as the sleeves were a bit too short.<ref name="SWHS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Yeah, well, as I've said, it's George Lucas' ugly child and people have fallen in love with it. And therefore it's no longer ugly&hellip; because love is in the eye of the beholder!|Lev Mailer, about ''The Star Wars Holiday Special''|<ref name="Interview" />}}
[[File:Lev_Mailer_headshot.jpg|thumb|150px|Lev Mailer portrayed the Imperial guard in ''The Star Wars Holiday Special''.]]
This Imperial guard appeared in the [[1978]] [[The Star Wars Holiday Special|''Star Wars Holiday Special'']], in which he was portrayed by [[Wikipedia:United States of America|American]] actor [[Lev Mailer]].<ref name="SWHS" /> In an interview with the fan site [[Starwarsholidayspecial.com]], Mailer explained that he and [[Art Carney]]&mdash;who portrayed Saun Dann&mdash;chose to play their scene like a classic "The Bully and The Idiot" routine, with Carney playing the idiot to his bully.<ref name="Interview">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsholidayspecial.com/text/lev_mailer.htm|text=Interview with Lev Mailer, "Imperial Guard #1"|author=SKot Kirkwood|date=2008-11-11|work=The Star Wars Holiday Special|archivedate=20170625083314}}</ref> The ''Holiday Special'' aired only once on television and was almost unanimously panned.<ref name="Jawa's Corner">{{InsiderCite|94|Jawa's Corner}}</ref><ref name="Bad Feeling">{{InsiderCite|106|I Have a Bad Feeling About This!}}</ref><ref name="farce1">{{WebCite|url=http://articles.latimes.com/2008/nov/16/entertainment/ca-starwars16|text=May the farce be with you (page 1 of 3)|work=[[Wikipedia:Los Angeles Times|Los Angeles Times]]|archivedate=20091010023132}}</ref> In an article published in the [[Star Wars Insider 106|106th issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine, ''[[Star Wars]]'' author [[Alex Newborn]] credited the Imperial characters as contributing factors to the program's lack of cohesion, calling them "ineffectual Imperial antagonists".<ref name="Bad Feeling" /> However, unlike other actors who starred in the show, Mailer didn't express regrets for participating in the ''Holiday Special'', stating it was "kind of a fun little show" and had "a certain charm."<ref name="Interview" />

In the show's credits, Mailer's character was credited as "Imperial Guard #1,"<ref name="SWHS" /> but the [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Emperor's Royal Guards]], also known as "Imperial Guards," first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], [[1983|five years]] after the ''Holiday Special''.<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Furthermore, the bully wears the distinctive helmet and black uniform of the [[Imperial Navy Trooper/Legends|Imperial Navy troopers]] who first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] in [[1977]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> However, the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Navy]] troopers had a wide range of duties, serving notably as guards aboard Imperial [[Battle station/Legends|battle stations]] such as the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="dbNT">{{DB|organization|imperialnavytrooper|Imperial Navy Troopers}}</ref> The presence of two [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinders]] in the small pockets of his tunic<ref name="SWHS" /> also indicates that the black guard was an officer and not just an enlisted [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]], since such devices were issued only to officers.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|88|Imperial code cylinder}}</ref> The mustachioed guard did not wear any [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank indicator plaque]].<ref name="SWHS" /> While officers with code cylinders and no plaque never appeared in the [[Original trilogy|''Star Wars'' trilogy]], some were seen in the [[1995]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault II: The Hidden Empire]]''.<ref name="RAII">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault II: The Hidden Empire]]''</ref>
